text:
sara: heads up — after merging the export-map change in @redwood/sdk@2.1.0 some of our node/cjs sample apps started failing in CI. stacktrace shows ESM text in CJS loader.

dan: can you paste the package.json snippet that caused it?

sara: sure, we switched to a minimal exports map to force the ESM entry for edge runtimes: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
This made `require('@redwood/sdk')` resolve to the mjs entry on node 14/16 runtime in our samples and yields `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`.

leo: ugh. customers and sample apps still do `const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk')` in lots of tutorials. We probably should not have removed a CJS path without a compatibility plan.

anika: Are types affected too? I remember a few TS samples doing `import sdk = require('@redwood/sdk')` which expects types aligned with CJS resolution.

sara: yep — our `types` pointer currently targets `dist/esm/index.d.ts`. Some TS toolchains (tsc + older bundlers) won't pick that up for `require()` style imports. So devs hit type errors in addition to runtime errors.

ci-bot: CI failure: onboarding-samples#992 on node 16 — sample-node-starter (exit 1)

dan: short-term: publish a patch that reintroduces a CJS export and uses conditional exports. example proposal: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
"module": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
```
That should preserve `require()` semantics while keeping ESM as default for modern bundlers/edges.

leo: agree. We should also ensure our build emits both `dist/cjs` and `dist/esm` and a single flattened `dist/index.d.ts` next to cjs entry so older consumers find typings.

anika: +1 on that. Also, one of the failing samples used our browser auth shim that expects a global fetch; the CJS node sample expected an injected runtime adapter. We should include a tiny auth parity check in smoke tests (node require/import + edge import) to catch runtime-only assumptions.

sara: plan: revert exports-only change in a 2.1.1 hotfix to unblock samples, then ship 2.1.2 with conditional exports, main/module/types fields, updated build pipeline, and CI smoke tests. I'll file the issue with the checklist and tag eng-devex and eng-runtime.

dan: also add a changelog blurb that mentions CJS consumers and how to migrate examples, and update docs samples to show both `require` and `import` patterns for the short term.

leo: for longer term, let's add a lightweight CI matrix that runs our sample apps in: node-require (node 14/16), node-import (node 18+), and edge-runtime (bun/vercel). That should catch regressions early.

ci-bot: created ticket #DEVEX-321: "restore CJS compatibility + conditional exports + smoke tests"

anika: thanks. can someone take the hotfix release? I'll volunteer to adjust the rollup/tsc config to output CJS + flattened d.ts.

sara: i'll cut the 2.1.1 revert PR and coordinate the release notes. tagging @release-squad.

dan: sounds good — thanks for catching this early via the onboarding sample CI.

leo: tiny follow-up — we should avoid changing package entry semantics without a release note that explicitly lists runtime compatibility (node versions, bundlers) so customers aren't surprised.

sara: agreed — adding that to the checklist for future export map changes. :memo:
